correctness.summary: With E=R-Id >= 0, Ge-Li-Li normalize H_1(E)=2 tr(E)/(n(n-1)). In even dimension their exact Pfaffian expansion and Chern-Gauss-Bonnet give omega_n-Vol = sum_{j>=1} binom(n/2,j) int H_j(E); in odd dimension their boundary-density expansion and nonnegative filling term give the corresponding inequality, with the non-strict case obtained by constant rescaling. Passing to the finite universal cover yields the reference volume omega_n/|pi_1|. The j=1 term is int tr(E)/(n-1), and positivity turns tr(E) into the Schatten-1 norm. The eigenform formula also gives H_j(E) >= lambda_min(E)^j, producing the nonlinear curvature-floor concentration law. Rescaled round spheres show the coefficient n-1 is first-order optimal, and in even dimensions they exactly saturate the nonlinear concentration bound.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The inspected Ge-Li-Li preprint proves the total scalar-curvature estimate and contains the positive curvature-polynomial expansions, but does not state the Bishop-deficit hierarchy, Schatten-norm stability, nonlinear curvature-floor concentration law, or sharp trace-norm constant. Related almost-maximal-volume and scalar-curvature-refined Bishop comparison results address metric/topological rigidity or scalar/Ricci information rather than this full curvature-operator L1 and higher-polynomial consequence. Targeted literature and current SCOPE searches did not locate an equivalent statement. Residual risk remains because the source theorem is extremely recent and the new theorem is a structural consequence of its proof identities.

value.summary: The result gives an explicit quantitative answer to the curvature-versus-volume mechanism motivating the source theorem: almost-maximal Bishop volume forces the complete curvature operator to approach the spherical operator in every Schatten L1 norm, with a sharp trace-norm coefficient. Retaining the higher positive Lipschitz-Killing terms yields a nonlinear bound on regions where the curvature-operator floor is stronger than spherical; in even dimensions the bound is exactly saturated by every round rescaling. The volume deficit is then an exact nonnegative curvature-excess budget.

limitations: The theorem requires the pointwise curvature-operator lower bound R >= Id, stronger than a Ricci lower bound.
No higher-Lp estimate for curvature magnitude is established here without additional geometric input.
The trace-norm coefficient and the even-dimensional nonlinear curvature-floor bound are sharp on round rescalings; the individual higher-order H_j bounds are not claimed optimal.
The odd-dimensional hierarchy is an inequality because the filling contributes a nonnegative interior Euler term.
The result is a structural consequence of the recent Ge-Li-Li theorem rather than an independent proof of that theorem.
The motivating theorem is extremely recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations remain a genuine originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
